requirements.requirement: Establish filesystem snapshot capability for /srv/data on node1 (native snapshot-capable filesystem backing the directory)
requirements.summary: Root filesystem is ext4 (no native snapshots), so executor installed btrfs-progs, created a loopback-backed btrfs filesystem with a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data, and persisted the mount via /etc/fstab, confirmed with mount -a and post-reboot auto-remount.

requirements.requirement: Capture a snapshot of /srv/data content at an earlier point in time
requirements.summary: Populated /srv/data with app.conf, record1.txt, record2.txt, then took a read-only btrfs snapshot and recorded a sha256 manifest of its contents.

requirements.requirement: Directory is subsequently modified (drift from the snapshot)
requirements.summary: app.conf was overwritten, record2.txt deleted, and junk.txt added; a diff against the baseline manifest confirms the drift.

requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Live subvolume was swapped for a writable snapshot of the read-only baseline; post-restore sha256 manifest diff against the baseline manifest is empty, and file listing shows junk.txt removed and record2.txt/app.conf restored.

overall_summary: The executor met the task contract: it established a real snapshot-capable filesystem (btrfs on a loopback device) backing /srv/data since the ext4 root offered no native snapshot support, captured a baseline snapshot, demonstrably modified the live directory, and restored it to byte-identical content matching the baseline snapshot via a verified sha256 manifest diff. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also completed correctly: pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state evidence, a reboot acknowledgement, connection drop/timeout during the transition, a new boot_id and fresh uptime post-restart, and a post-reboot verification that /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab with content still matching the baseline manifest — this aligns with the fixed before/after boot-identity cross-check. Minor hygiene residue (leftover /tmp manifest/log files and an unremoved old btrfs subvolume) was left behind but is low-risk and does not affect functional correctness.
limitations: No independent inspection of the live btrfs filesystem was possible beyond the captured command outputs; all conclusions rely on executor-reported sha256 manifests and subvolume listings.

The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not include a distinct after_prepare capture (prepare was disabled), so preparer- vs executor-caused state could not be separated via that channel, though this had no material effect since prepare added nothing.

operational_hygiene.summary: Setup involved a few corrected missteps (an initial failed losetup attempt in cmd-d4bcf48e6611404f re-run successfully in cmd-70ee206a9c7549dd; an OpenRC local.d startup script created in cmd-5b3dbd3dbf4b4cf0 then deliberately removed in favor of /etc/fstab in cmd-3f3bc0d51ae14993 — a reasonable design correction, not residue). Remaining unnecessary residue: several manifest/log files were left under /tmp (baseline_manifest.txt, modified_manifest.txt, postboot_manifest.txt, restored_manifest.txt, snap_path.env, reboot.log — confirmed in the after_executor temporary-files diff) that were not cleaned up after verification completed; these are low-risk, bounded artifacts but were retained rather than removed. The old pre-restore btrfs subvolume (data-corrupted-*, visible in cmd-ce131752e18a469e and cmd-3db48b74193946e4 subvolume listings) was also left on disk rather than deleted, consuming minor space but posing no security or functional risk. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations occurred; package state is healthy (chrony.drift entry is pre-existing, unchanged before/after).
